```{r}
# ---- Presentation helpers -------------------------------------------------------
callout <- function(type, title, body, collapse = FALSE) {
  cat(sprintf("\n::: {.callout-%s%s}\n## %s\n\n%s\n:::\n\n", type,
              if (collapse) ' collapse="true"' else "", title, paste(body, collapse = "\n\n")))
}

download_link <- function(path, label, mime = NULL) {
  if (is.na(path) || !file.exists(path)) return(invisible(NULL))
  uri <- base64enc::dataURI(file = path, mime = mime %||% mime_for(path))
  knitr::asis_output(sprintf('\n<a class="fw-download" download="%s" href="%s">&#11015; %s</a>\n',
                             basename(path), uri, label))
}
mime_for <- function(path) {
  switch(tolower(tools::file_ext(path)),
         png = "image/png", csv = "text/csv", json = "application/json",
         parquet = "application/octet-stream", gpkg = "application/geopackage+sqlite3",
         zip = "application/zip", mp4 = "video/mp4", "application/octet-stream")
}

figure_files <- character()
table_files <- character()

# Print a ggplot, save it to outs/figures, and add an embedded download link.
show_fig <- function(plot, name, width = 10, height = 6) {
  path <- file.path(paths$figures_dir, paste0(name, ".png"))
  ggsave(path, plot, width = width, height = height, dpi = p$figure_dpi, bg = "white")
  figure_files <<- unique(c(figure_files, path))
  print(plot)
  fig_link(name)
}

# Download link for the figure shown just above. The link saves the image that
# is already on the page (see the script at the end of the document), so the
# figure is not embedded twice.
fig_link <- function(name) {
  knitr::asis_output(sprintf('\n<a class="fw-download fw-fig-download" href="#" data-filename="%s.png">&#11015; Download figure (PNG)</a>\n', name))
}

# Interactive table with Copy / CSV / Excel buttons; also saved to outs/tables.
dt <- function(data, name = NULL, page_length = 10, caption = NULL, filter = NULL) {
  file_stub <- name %||% "carolina_highground_table"
  if (!is.null(name)) {
    path <- file.path(paths$tables_dir, paste0(name, ".csv"))
    readr::write_csv(data, path, na = "")
    table_files <<- unique(c(table_files, path))
  }
  DT::datatable(
    data,
    rownames = FALSE,
    class = "display compact stripe",
    caption = caption,
    extensions = "Buttons",
    filter = filter %||% (if (nrow(data) > 25) "top" else "none"),
    options = list(
      pageLength = page_length,
      scrollX = TRUE,
      dom = "Bfrtip",
      buttons = list(
        list(extend = "copy", text = "Copy"),
        list(extend = "csv", text = "CSV", filename = file_stub),
        list(extend = "excel", text = "Excel", filename = file_stub)
      )
    )
  )
}

stat_cards <- function(values, labels, alert = rep(FALSE, length(values))) {
  cards <- paste0('<div class="stat-card', ifelse(alert, " alert", ""), '"><div class="stat-value">',
                  values, '</div><div class="stat-label">', labels, "</div></div>", collapse = "")
  cat('\n<div class="stat-grid">', cards, "</div>\n\n", sep = "")
}

dataset_card <- function(...) {
  items <- list(...)
  rows <- paste0("<tr><td>", names(items), "</td><td>", unlist(items), "</td></tr>", collapse = "")
  cat('\n<div class="dataset-card"><table>', rows, "</table></div>\n\n", sep = "")
}

comma <- scales::comma
dollars_short <- function(x) scales::dollar(x, scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale(), accuracy = 0.1)
```

# Why Carolina HighGround {#sec-why}

::: {.lead-text}
Floods are measured in dollars and event counts, but people live them as lost homes, cut-off roads, and neighbors who didn't make it out. Carolina HighGround uses public data to show **where storm impacts on people are most severe in Western North Carolina, and why**, so that communities, emergency planners, and infrastructure agencies can direct attention before the next storm rather than after it.
:::

```{r}
#| label: story-cards
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

if (story$hl_events > 0) {
  stat_cards(
    values = c(comma(story$hl_deaths), dollars_short(story$hl_damage), comma(story$hl_events),
               scales::percent(story$hl_death_share, accuracy = 1)),
    labels = c(sprintf("deaths recorded by NOAA in the study counties during %s (%s to %s)", p$highlight_event_name,
                       format(hl_window[1], "%b %d"), format(hl_window[2], "%b %d, %Y")),
               sprintf("reported property + crop damage in the study counties during %s", p$highlight_event_name),
               sprintf("NOAA storm events logged in those counties that week (%s flood-related)", story$hl_flood),
               sprintf("of all storm deaths recorded in the study counties, %s-%s", p$start_year, p$end_year)),
    alert = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)
  )
}
```

## The problem

In late September 2024, the remnants of **`r p$highlight_event_name`** stalled over the Blue Ridge. Rain fell for days on steep, saturated slopes. Rivers and small creeks rose into towns built along their banks, debris flows cut off mountain communities, and roads, bridges, and culverts failed when people needed them most.

The numbers above come straight from the NOAA Storm Events records analyzed in this report. In the `r length(p$study_counties)` study counties (`r paste(p$study_counties, collapse = ", ")`), that single week accounts for **`r scales::percent(story$hl_death_share, accuracy = 1)` of the storm deaths** and **`r scales::percent(story$hl_damage_share, accuracy = 1)` of the reported damage** across `r p$start_year`-`r p$end_year`. In the mountains, a rare event can outweigh a decade of ordinary storms. That makes it hard to plan for, and it is why we need to understand the *places* that make an event deadly, not just the storms themselves.

## In their words: growing up through Helene in Asheville

## Our question and approach

> **Which storm events in North Carolina become high-consequence (deadly or very costly), and what features of the landscape and built environment around them (steep terrain, nearby streams, road crossings, paved surfaces) help explain it?**

We answer this in four steps. Each step is one section of this report.

## Preprocessing

### One row per storm event

The three NOAA tables can't simply be joined together. One event can have several fatality rows (one per person) and several location rows. A naive join repeats that event's deaths, injuries, and damage once per matching row, and summing afterwards inflates the totals. Our pipeline instead:

* collapses the **details** table to one row per `EVENT_ID`, taking `max()` of the impacts (never a sum) and the first non-missing value of the metadata;
* aggregates **fatalities** separately into per-event record counts;
* aggregates **locations** separately, keeping a record count and the first point as a coordinate fallback.

```{r}
#| label: noaa-code
#| ref.label: prepare-noaa
#| eval: false
```

```{r}
#| label: noaa-dup-table
knitr::kable(prep$duplication_checks, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
             caption = "Rows per EVENT_ID before and after processing")
```

```{r}
#| label: noaa-dup-assert
#| echo: false

after <- dplyr::filter(prep$duplication_checks, stringr::str_detect(table, "after"))
if (after$max_rows_per_event == 1 && after$duplicated_events == 0) {
  callout("tip", "Validation passed: exactly one row per event",
          sprintf("%s events, %s distinct `EVENT_ID`s: `max_rows_per_event = 1`, `duplicate_events = 0`. As the table shows, the raw fatalities and locations tables have up to %s and %s rows per event, which is why they are aggregated separately.",
                  comma(after$rows), comma(after$distinct_event_ids),
                  prep$duplication_checks$max_rows_per_event[2], prep$duplication_checks$max_rows_per_event[3]))
}
```

As a consistency check, we compared deaths in the details table with the number of fatality records. Differences are reported, not overwritten:

```{r}
#| label: noaa-fatality-consistency
#| echo: false
knitr::kable(prep$fatality_consistency, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

### Assigning North Carolina regions

NOAA records events either by **county** (`CZ_TYPE = "C"`) or by **National Weather Service forecast zone** (`CZ_TYPE = "Z"`, e.g. *INLAND PENDER*, *BURKE MOUNTAINS*, *HATTERAS ISLAND*). A zone's `CZ_FIPS` is a zone number, not a county code, so zones are matched by name. Each record gets the first rule that succeeds, and the rule used is stored with it:

| Method | Rule |
|---|---|
| `exact_county_match` | County record matched on its 3-digit FIPS, or a zone name that is exactly a county name |
| `forecast_zone_county_match` | Zone name matches a county after removing descriptors such as *Western*, *Inland*, *Greater*, *Mountains* |
| `special_coastal_zone` | Barrier-island zones with no county in the name (*Outer Banks*, *Ocracoke*, *Hatteras*) |
| `unmatched` | Left without a region; never defaulted to a region |

```{r}
#| label: region-summary
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
event_level |>
  dplyr::count(region_assignment_method, region, name = "events") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = region, values_from = events, values_fill = 0) |>
  knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","), caption = "Events by assignment method and region") |>
  print()
unmatched <- dplyr::filter(prep$region_assignments, region_assignment_method == "unmatched")
if (nrow(unmatched) > 0) {
  callout("warning", sprintf("%d unmatched zone name(s)", nrow(unmatched)), paste0("`", unique(unmatched$CZ_NAME), "`", collapse = ", "))
} else {
  callout("tip", "Every county and zone record was matched", "No record fell through to `unmatched`.")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: region-zone-table
prep$region_assignments |>
  dplyr::filter(region_assignment_method != "exact_county_match") |>
  dplyr::select(CZ_TYPE, CZ_FIPS, CZ_NAME, region, region_assignment_method, matched_county) |>
  dplyr::arrange(region_assignment_method, CZ_NAME) |>
  dt(name = "forecast_zone_matches", page_length = 8)
```

```{r}
} else NULL

  sf::st_read(paths$county_boundaries, quiet = TRUE) |>

    dplyr::mutate(in_study = county_name %in% toupper(p$study_counties))
} else {

         paste("Not found at", display_path(paths$county_boundaries, project_dir), "- maps use the state outline only."), "maps")

}
study_counties_sf <- if (!is.null(counties)) dplyr::filter(counties, in_study) else NULL
study_bbox <- if (!is.null(study_counties_sf) && nrow(study_counties_sf) > 0) sf::st_bbox(sf::st_buffer(sf::st_union(study_counties_sf), 3000)) else NULL
```

## What NOAA can't tell us, and why we added more data

```{r}
#| label: gap-numbers
#| include: false
gap <- list(
  no_coords = mean(is.na(event_level$longitude)),
  zone_no_coords = mean(is.na(event_level$longitude[event_level$cz_type == "Z"])),
  flood_coords = mean(!is.na(event_level$longitude[event_level$is_flood_event == 1])),
  rare = mean(event_level$total_deaths > 0)
)
```

NOAA tells us **what** happened, **when**, and **how bad** it was. It does not tell us **why** one creek crossing became deadly while a similar storm a few miles away did little harm. Three gaps stand out:

1. **Outcomes, not conditions.** The records describe the storm and its toll, not the ground it fell on: slope, how close homes and roads are to streams, whether water can soak in or runs off pavement.
2. **Rare, extreme harm.** Only `r scales::percent(gap$rare, accuracy = 0.1)` of events caused a death. A model needs place-based context to tell a routine storm from a deadly one.
3. **Location detail varies.** `r scales::percent(gap$no_coords, accuracy = 1)` of events (mostly forecast-zone records) have no coordinates, but `r scales::percent(gap$flood_coords, accuracy = 1)` of flood-related events do. For those events we can measure the landscape around the exact point where the event was reported.

Each gap maps to a public dataset:

| Question NOAA can't answer | Dataset we added | What it measures around each event |
|---|---|---|
| Was the event near a stream or river? | **USGS NHD High Resolution** (+ WBD watersheds) | distance to nearest stream, stream counts and density, containing HUC12 |
| Was the ground steep or rugged? | **USGS 3DEP-derived elevation, slope, roughness** | elevation, slope, and roughness at the point and nearby |
| Were roads crossing water nearby? | **NCDOT bridges/structures and culverts** | distance to and count of nearby crossings |
| Was the land paved or natural? | **USGS Annual NLCD imperviousness** | % impervious surface at and around the point |
| Would the soil absorb water? | **USDA SSURGO** | statewide soil summary (not yet mappable to events) |
| How much rain actually fell? | **gridMET daily precipitation** | event-window total, wettest day, and the prior 7 days |
| How low is the ground relative to the stream, and how big is the stream? | **DEM hydrology (WhiteboxTools)** | height above nearest stream (HAND) and upstream drainage area |
| Who lives there? | **CDC/ATSDR SVI (census tracts)** | tract social-vulnerability percentiles |

```{r}
  Contents = sprintf("Elevation (m), slope (degrees), and terrain roughness (m), clipped to North Carolina and projected to EPSG:%s at %s m cells", p$analysis_crs, dem_res),
  "Why we use it" = "Steep, rugged terrain speeds runoff, feeds flash floods and debris flows, and isolates communities",
  "How we use it" = sprintf("Value at the event point and mean within %s", eb),
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-terrain
#| fig-height: 5.5
raster_df <- function(path, fact, crop_to = NULL) {
  r <- terra::rast(path)[[1]]
  if (!is.null(crop_to)) r <- terra::crop(r, terra::project(terra::vect(crop_to), terra::crs(r)), mask = TRUE)
  if (fact > 1) r <- terra::aggregate(r, fact = fact, fun = "mean", na.rm = TRUE)
  df <- as.data.frame(r, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
  names(df)[3] <- "value"
  list(df = df, crs = terra::crs(r))
}
if (file.exists(paths$dem) && file.exists(paths$slope)) {
  elev <- raster_df(paths$dem, fact = 8, crop_to = nc_boundary)
  g1 <- ggplot(elev$df, aes(x, y, fill = value)) + geom_raster() +
    scale_fill_gradientn(colors = terrain.colors(10), name = "Elevation (m)") +
    coord_sf(crs = elev$crs, datum = NA) +
    labs(title = "Elevation across North Carolina") + map_theme + theme(legend.key.width = unit(1.3, "cm"))
  slope <- raster_df(paths$slope, fact = 2, crop_to = study_counties_sf)
  g2 <- ggplot(slope$df, aes(x, y, fill = value)) + geom_raster() +
    geom_sf(data = study_counties_sf, inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = NA, color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "rocket", direction = -1, name = "Slope (degrees)") +
    coord_sf(crs = slope$crs, datum = NA) +
    labs(title = "Slope in the study counties") + map_theme + theme(legend.key.width = unit(1.3, "cm"))
  g <- (g1 | g2) + plot_layout(widths = c(1.6, 1)) +
    plot_annotation(caption = "Source: elevatr / AWS Terrain Tiles (USGS 3DEP in the U.S.)")
  show_fig(g, "09_terrain", 13, 5.5)
}
```

```{r}
                     if (isTRUE(p$nlcd_year_matched)) "2016-2023" else p$nlcd_vintage, nlcd_res),
  "Why we use it" = "Pavement and rooftops shed water quickly, raising flood peaks in developed valleys",
  "How we use it" = sprintf("Value at the event point and means within %s and %s, taken from the layer for the event's own year", eb, ib),
  Caveats = "Events after 2023 use the 2023 layer (the latest available); the service export cap made cells coarser than native 30 m"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-soils
#| fig-height: 4.5
if (file.exists(soil_file)) {
  soils <- readr::read_csv(soil_file, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::mutate(county = toupper(stringr::str_remove(areaname, " County, North Carolina$")),
                  area = dplyr::if_else(county %in% toupper(p$study_counties), "Study counties", "Rest of NC"),
                  comppct_r = as.numeric(comppct_r))
  share <- function(var) {
    soils |>
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[var]])) |>
      dplyr::group_by(area, value = .data[[var]]) |>
      dplyr::summarise(weight = sum(comppct_r, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(share = weight / sum(weight)) |>
      dplyr::ungroup()
  }
  area_fill <- scale_fill_manual(values = c("Study counties" = fw_colors$teal, "Rest of NC" = "gray70"), name = NULL)
  g1 <- ggplot(share("hydgrp"), aes(value, share, fill = area)) + geom_col(position = "dodge") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + area_fill +
    labs(title = "Hydrologic soil group", subtitle = "A = high infiltration ... D = very low", x = NULL, y = NULL)
  g2 <- share("drainagecl") |>
    ggplot(aes(share, reorder(value, share), fill = area)) + geom_col(position = "dodge") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + area_fill +
    labs(title = "Drainage class", x = NULL, y = NULL)
  g <- (g1 | g2) + plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  g <- g + plot_annotation(caption = "Share of component percent within survey areas (not area-weighted). Source: USDA NRCS SSURGO")
  show_fig(g, "12_ssurgo_summary", 12, 4.8)
}
```

```{r}
  }
```

```{r}
    check_input(paths$community, "Community vulnerability", FALSE, "county CSV with `county_fips` + numeric columns", "community features", project_dir)) {

  if ("county_fips" %in% names(comm)) {

      dplyr::left_join(comm, by = "matched_county_fips") |> dplyr::select(-matched_county_fips)
    optional_feature_cols <- c(optional_feature_cols, setdiff(names(comm), "matched_county_fips"))

}

}
```

# Bringing the Data Together {#sec-integration}

## One coordinate system, clean geometry

The inputs arrive in four coordinate systems: WGS 84 (NOAA, NCDOT), NAD83 (NHD, WBD), NC State Plane (terrain), and CONUS Albers (NLCD). Every vector layer goes through the same three steps before any spatial operation:

1. `st_zm()` drops Z/M dimensions. NHD flowlines are stored as `3D Measured` (XYZM), which GEOS cannot process.
2. `st_make_valid()` repairs invalid geometries.
3. `st_transform()` projects to **EPSG:`r p$analysis_crs`** (NAD83 / North Carolina, meters), where all distances and buffers are measured.

Rasters are **never resampled**. Instead, event points and buffers are projected into each raster's own CRS for extraction, so the original cell values are preserved.

## Features measured around every event

```{r}
#| label: feature-method-table
#| echo: false
tibble::tribble(

  "Watershed", "WBD", "huc12, huc12_area_km2", "Subwatershed polygon containing the point (membership only)",
  "Road crossings", "NCDOT", sprintf("distance_to_nearest_culvert_m / structure_m, culverts_/structures_within_%s and _%s", eb, ib), "Nearest-point distance; count within buffer",
  "Terrain", "3DEP-derived", sprintf("elevation_m, slope_degrees, terrain_roughness, *_mean_%s", eb), "Cell value at point; mean of cells in buffer",
  "Imperviousness", "Annual NLCD (year-matched)", sprintf("impervious_mean_event, impervious_mean_%s, impervious_mean_%s", eb, ib), "Cell value at point; mean of cells in buffer (0-100 %), from the event year's layer",
  "Hydrology", "DEM + WhiteboxTools", sprintf("hand_m, drainage_area_km2_max_%s, log_drainage_area_km2", eb), "HAND at point; largest upstream drainage area in buffer",
  "Tract vulnerability", "CDC/ATSDR SVI", "svi_rpl_themes, svi_rpl_theme1-4", "Tract containing the point; latest release at or before the event year",
  "Rainfall", "gridMET", "rain_event_total_mm, rain_max_1day_mm, rain_antecedent_7d_mm", "Daily cell values summed or maxed over the event window"
```

```{r}
#| label: spatial-features
scope_filter <- switch(
  p$feature_event_scope,
  all               = rep(TRUE, nrow(event_level)),
  flood             = event_level$is_flood_event == 1,
  flood_or_tropical = event_level$is_flood_event == 1 | event_level$is_tropical_event == 1,
  stop("feature_event_scope must be one of: all, flood, flood_or_tropical")
)
events_in_scope <- event_level[scope_filter, ]

spatial_settings <- list(
  analysis_crs = p$analysis_crs, geographic_crs = p$geographic_crs,
  event_buffer_m = p$event_buffer_m, stream_buffer_m = p$stream_buffer_m,
  infrastructure_buffer_m = p$infrastructure_buffer_m,
  nhd_flowline_ftypes = unlist(p$nhd_flowline_ftypes), compute_stream_density = p$compute_stream_density,
  include_nhd_features = p$include_nhd_features, include_wbd_features = p$include_wbd_features,
  include_ncdot_features = p$include_ncdot_features, include_dem_features = p$include_dem_features,
  include_nlcd_features = p$include_nlcd_features, nlcd_vintage = p$nlcd_vintage,
  nlcd_year_matched = isTRUE(p$nlcd_year_matched),
  include_hydro_features = isTRUE(p$include_hydro_features),
  include_svi_features = isTRUE(p$include_svi_features)
)

spatial <- cached_spatial_features(
  events_in_scope,
  inputs      = paths[c("nhd_zip", "nhd_dir", "ncdot_culverts", "ncdot_structures", "dem", "slope", "roughness", "nlcd",
                        "hydro_dir", "svi_dir", "tracts_2010", "tracts_2020")],
  settings    = spatial_settings,
  cache_dir   = paths$derived_dir,
  use_cache   = isTRUE(p$use_cached_features),
  refresh     = isTRUE(p$refresh_derived_data),
  project_dir = project_dir
)
feature_cols <- setdiff(names(spatial$features), "event_id")
```

## Input validation

```{r}
#| label: spatial-layers
raster_row <- function(path, dataset) {
  if (is.na(path) || !file.exists(path)) return(tibble::tibble(dataset = dataset, file = basename(path), crs = NA, cell_size_m = NA, cells = NA))
  r <- terra::rast(path)
  tibble::tibble(dataset = dataset, file = basename(path), crs = paste0("EPSG:", terra::crs(r, describe = TRUE)$code),
                 cell_size_m = round(terra::res(r)[1], 1), cells = comma(terra::ncell(r)))
}
layer_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  spatial$layer_summary |> dplyr::transmute(dataset, file, crs, geometry_before_cleaning = geometry_type, features = comma(features)),
  dplyr::bind_rows(raster_row(paths$dem, "DEM"), raster_row(paths$slope, "Slope"), raster_row(paths$roughness, "Roughness"),
                   raster_row(paths$nlcd, paste("NLCD imperviousness", p$nlcd_vintage))) |>
    dplyr::transmute(dataset, file, crs, geometry_before_cleaning = paste0("raster, ", cell_size_m, " m cells"), features = cells)
)
dt(layer_table, name = "spatial_input_validation", page_length = 10)
```

## Assembling the event-level table

```{r}
#| label: targets-and-assembly
event_level <- event_level |>
  dplyr::mutate(split = assign_split(event_year, p$train_end_year, p$validation_end_year))

targets <- add_targets(event_level,
                       damage_quantile      = p$damage_quantile,
                       positive_damage_only = p$target_positive_damage_only,
                       death_target_value   = p$death_target_value,
                       threshold_basis      = p$target_threshold_basis)
event_level <- targets$events

noaa_dates <- range(noaa_inventory$creation_date)
vintages <- list(
  noaa  = sprintf("NOAA Storm Events %s-%s (file revisions %s to %s)", p$start_year, p$end_year, noaa_dates[1], noaa_dates[2]),
  nhd   = if (!is.na(nhd_date)) sprintf("NHD HR state extract (flowlines dated %s)", nhd_date) else "NHD HR state extract",
  ncdot = if (!is.na(ncdot_date)) sprintf("NCDOT Structures service (retrieved %s)", ncdot_date) else "NCDOT Structures service",
  dem   = "elevatr AWS terrain tiles (3DEP in US)",
  nlcd  = if (isTRUE(p$nlcd_year_matched)) "Annual NLCD, year-matched 2016-2023 (later events use 2023)" else paste("Annual NLCD", p$nlcd_vintage, "(static)"),
  rain  = "gridMET daily precipitation, 2016-2026 files",
  svi   = "CDC/ATSDR SVI tract releases 2016/2018/2020/2022"
)
row_vintage <- paste(c(vintages$noaa, if (p$include_nhd_features) vintages$nhd, if (p$include_ncdot_features) vintages$ncdot,
                       if (p$include_dem_features) vintages$dem, if (p$include_nlcd_features) vintages$nlcd,
                       if (isTRUE(p$include_rainfall_features)) vintages$rain, if (isTRUE(p$include_svi_features)) vintages$svi), collapse = "; ")

model_table <- event_level |>
  dplyr::left_join(spatial$features, by = "event_id") |>
  dplyr::left_join(optional_features, by = "event_id")
# Columns used by the coverage flags may be absent when their feature group is off.
for (nm in c("impervious_vintage", "hydro_basin_crosses_state")) {
  if (!nm %in% names(model_table)) model_table[[nm]] <- NA_integer_
}
model_table <- model_table |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    has_features = event_id %in% spatial$features$event_id,
    spatial_feature_method = dplyr::if_else(has_features, "point_buffer (no catchment/upstream area)", "none"),
    source_vintage = row_vintage,
    data_coverage_warning = purrr::pmap_chr(
      list(has_features, event_coordinate_quality, is_partial_year, cz_type, event_id %in% events_in_scope$event_id,
           impervious_vintage, event_year, hydro_basin_crosses_state),
      function(has, quality, partial, cz, in_scope, imp_v, ev_year, crosses) {
        flags <- c(if (!in_scope) "outside_feature_scope",
                   if (in_scope && !has) paste0("no_usable_coordinates(", quality, ")"),
                   if (partial) "partial_year",
                   if (cz == "Z") "forecast_zone_record",
                   if (has && p$include_ncdot_features) "ncdot_inventory_may_be_incomplete",
                   if (has && p$include_nlcd_features && !is.na(imp_v) && !is.na(ev_year) && imp_v != ev_year) paste0("nlcd_vintage_", imp_v),
                   if (has && isTRUE(crosses == 1)) "drainage_area_truncated_at_state_line")
        if (length(flags) == 0) "none" else paste(flags, collapse = "; ")
      })
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(-has_features)

roles <- column_roles(feature_cols, optional_feature_cols)
model_table <- dplyr::select(model_table, dplyr::any_of(c(roles$identifier, roles$context, roles$predictor, roles$outcome, roles$target)))

final_check <- duplication_check(model_table, "model table", "event_id")
stopifnot(final_check$max_rows_per_event == 1, final_check$duplicated_events == 0)
```

The combined table has **`r comma(nrow(model_table))` rows** (one per storm event) and **`r ncol(model_table)` columns**. NOAA narratives are left out because they describe the outcomes.

The figures below are descriptive comparisons, not model results.

```{r}

  dplyr::group_by(event_year, region) |>
  dplyr::summarise(events = dplyr::n(), rate = mean(high_consequence)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(region = factor(region, region_levels, region_labels))
g <- ggplot(balance, aes(event_year, rate, color = region)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(aes(size = events)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = region_colors, name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = years) +
  labs(title = "How often events become high-consequence",
       subtitle = sprintf("Share of events with a death or damage above %s (%s)", dollars_short(targets$threshold), p$target_threshold_basis),
       x = NULL, y = NULL, size = "Events", caption = noaa_caption)
show_fig(g, "14_high_consequence_rate", 10, 5)
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-correlation
```

# Machine-Learning-Ready Data {#sec-ml}

## Outcome labels

```{r}
#| label: target-table
targets$definitions |>
  dplyr::transmute(target_name, definition,
                   damage_threshold = scales::dollar(damage_threshold_dollars),
                   positives, prevalence = scales::percent(prevalence, accuracy = 0.1), leakage_warning) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Leakage rules for the modeling team
* **Damage threshold:** `r if (p$target_threshold_basis == "train_split") sprintf("computed from training years only (%s), so the target is leakage-safe as exported.", scales::dollar(targets$threshold)) else sprintf("computed on all events (%s). Recompute it on training rows only before final evaluation; the formula is in target_config.json.", scales::dollar(targets$threshold))`
* **Never use outcome columns as predictors**: deaths, injuries, damage, `any_*`, fatality-record counts, or the damage-reported flags. The feature dictionary marks each column's role.
* **Split by time** using the `split` column, and group cross-validation folds by `episode_id` so events from one storm stay together.
* **Leave spatial NAs as missing.** They mean "no coordinates", not "zero".
* **Imperviousness post-dates most events** (`r p$nlcd_vintage` layer). Check how much the model depends on it.
:::

## Recommended chronological split

```{r}
#| label: split-summary
split_summary <- model_table |>
  dplyr::group_by(split, event_year, is_partial_year) |>
  dplyr::summarise(events = dplyr::n(), with_coordinates = sum(!is.na(longitude)),
                   high_consequence = sum(high_consequence), high_human_impact = sum(high_human_impact)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::arrange(event_year)
dt(split_summary, name = "split_recommendation", page_length = 12)
```

## Feature dictionary

```{r}
#| label: dictionary
dictionary <- build_feature_dictionary(model_table, roles, spatial_settings, vintages)
dictionary |>
  dplyr::select(column_name, role, units, description, source_dataset, leakage_warning) |>
  dt(name = "feature_dictionary", page_length = 12, filter = "top")
```

## Exported files

```{r}
#| label: ml-export
target_config <- list(
  target_name = p$target_name, damage_quantile = p$damage_quantile,
  positive_damage_only = p$target_positive_damage_only, death_target_value = p$death_target_value,
  threshold_basis = p$target_threshold_basis, damage_threshold_dollars = targets$threshold,
  train_end_year = p$train_end_year, validation_end_year = p$validation_end_year,
  partial_years = unlist(p$partial_years),
  recompute_instructions = "threshold = quantile(total_damage[split == 'train' & total_damage > 0], damage_quantile); high_consequence = (total_deaths >= death_target_value) | (total_damage > threshold)"
)
manifest <- list(
  created = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z"),
  params = p[setdiff(names(p), "project_dir")],
  rows = nrow(model_table), columns = ncol(model_table),
  spatial_methods = spatial$methods, coverage_notes = spatial$coverage,
  vintages = vintages, pipeline_log = fw_log_table(), r_version = R.version.string
)
# Guard: never overwrite the ML handoff with degraded data. If a feature group
# that is switched on came out entirely empty (e.g. its input files were not
# found), the export is skipped unless allow_degraded_export is TRUE.
feature_groups <- feature_column_names(spatial_settings)
enabled_groups <- c(nhd = p$include_nhd_features, wbd = p$include_wbd_features, ncdot = p$include_ncdot_features,
                    dem = p$include_dem_features, nlcd = p$include_nlcd_features,
                    hydro = isTRUE(p$include_hydro_features), svi = isTRUE(p$include_svi_features))
located_rows <- !is.na(model_table$longitude)
degraded_groups <- names(enabled_groups)[enabled_groups & vapply(names(enabled_groups), function(g) {
  cols <- intersect(feature_groups[[g]], names(model_table))
  length(cols) == 0 || all(is.na(as.matrix(model_table[located_rows, cols])))
}, logical(1))]

if (length(degraded_groups) > 0 && !isTRUE(p$allow_degraded_export)) {
  fw_log("error", "ML export", paste("Skipped: feature group(s) entirely missing:", paste(degraded_groups, collapse = ", "),
                                     "- check the input paths. Existing files in", display_path(paths$ml_dir, project_dir), "were left unchanged."),
         "ML export")
  ml_files <- tibble::tibble(file = character(), rows = integer(), columns = integer(), exists = logical(), size_mb = numeric())
} else {
  ml_files <- export_ml_tables(
    model_table, roles, dictionary, targets$definitions, target_config, split_summary,
    ml_dir = paths$ml_dir, export_csv = p$export_csv, export_parquet = p$export_parquet,
    export_spatial_layer = p$export_spatial_layer, export_feature_dictionary = p$export_feature_dictionary,
    analysis_crs = p$analysis_crs, geographic_crs = p$geographic_crs, manifest = manifest
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: ml-export-guard
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (length(degraded_groups) > 0 && !isTRUE(p$allow_degraded_export)) {
  callout("important", "ML files were NOT written",
          sprintf("These enabled feature groups came out entirely missing: **%s**. That almost always means their input files were not found (see the input inventory in the appendix). The existing files in `%s` were left unchanged.",
                  paste(degraded_groups, collapse = ", "), display_path(paths$ml_dir, project_dir)))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: ml-files
#| echo: false
file_purpose <- c(
  nc_storm_event_model_table = "All events: identifiers, context, predictors, outcomes, targets, split",
  nc_flood_event_model_table = "Flood-related events only: the main table for a flood model",
  nc_storm_predictors_only = "Identifiers + predictors only (no outcomes)",
  nc_storm_targets = "Identifiers + outcomes + targets",
  feature_dictionary = "Role, units, source, and leakage note for every column",
  target_definitions = "Target rules, threshold, and prevalence",
  split_recommendation = "Events and positives per year and split",
  target_config = "Target settings and recompute formula (JSON)",
  nc_storm_event_features = "Events as map points (GeoPackage, EPSG:32119)",
  run_manifest = "Parameters, data vintages, and pipeline log for this run"
)
ml_files |>
  dplyr::filter(exists) |>
  dplyr::transmute(file = display_path(file, project_dir),
                   purpose = unname(file_purpose[tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(file))]),
                   rows, columns, size_mb) |>
  dt(page_length = 20)
```

Every file above was confirmed on disk after writing. The core files are bundled as **carolina_highground_ml_ready.zip** in [Downloads](#sec-downloads).
